# ya-runtime-vm 0.6.1-rc1

This release candidate hardens the embedded OpenVMM virtio devices and host
runtime against guest-triggered denial-of-service, replaces host Unix domain
sockets for guest-agent communication with in-process memory streams, and
migrates Unix syscall wrappers in the runtime from `libc` to `rustix`.

## Changes

- **In-memory guest-agent vsock transport**: replace host Unix domain sockets
  and `/tmp` socket directories with an in-process memory stream (`MemoryStream`
  / `RelaySocket::pair` and `VirtioVsockDevice::new_in_memory`), rejecting any
  guest connection attempts to ports other than `GUEST_AGENT_VSOCK_PORT` (`1024`).
- **Virtio queue and device bounds (`patches/openvmm/hypervisor-cpuid.patch`)**:
  - `virtio`: reject indirect descriptor tables whose entry count would overflow
    `u16` (`QueueError::TooLong`) and reject nested `VIRTIO_DESC_F_INDIRECT` on
    entry `0` of an indirect table (`QueueError::DoubleIndirect`).
  - `virtio_blk`: cap per-request `data_len` at `16 MiB` and slow-path bounce
    buffer allocations at `254 * 4096` bytes.
  - `virtio_vsock`: cap host-to-guest slow-path bounce buffer allocations in
    `handle_host_data` to `min(peer_free, TX_BUF_SIZE)`.
  - `virtiofs`: check `offset + 4 <= config.len()` in `read_registers_u32` so
    unaligned reads near the end of the config space return `0` instead of
    panicking.
- **Network TX and event queue bounds**:
  - `virtio_net`: reject TX descriptor chains larger than `65553` bytes before
    linearizing into a host buffer.
  - `net_socket`: bound TX frame size (`65535` bytes) and pending TX queue depth
    (`256` frames).
  - `guest_agent_comm` & `vmrt`: bound the guest notification channel (`256`
    events) and process exit output drain iterations (`64` chunks per stream).
- **Input validation and host process hardening**:
  - Cap `.gvmi` footer `json_len` at `1 MiB` before allocation and reject
    whitespace, control characters, or quotes in kernel command-line tokens.
  - Replace direct `unsafe { libc::... }` calls in `crates/runtime` with safe
    `rustix` wrappers.
  - Enable `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` and install a thread-synchronized (`SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_TSYNC`)
    seccomp-BPF filter via `seccompiler` on Linux before launching the VM worker,
    blocking new socket creation and connections (`socket`, `socketpair`, `bind`,
    `listen`, `connect`), process execution (`execve`/`execveat`/`fork`/`vfork`),
    filesystem links/device nodes/permission/mount manipulation (`symlink*`,
    `link*`, `mknod*`, `chmod*`, `chown*`, `mount`, `chroot`, `pivot_root`,
    `open_by_handle_at`), and kernel attack surface syscalls (`ptrace`, `bpf`,
    `userfaultfd`, `perf_event_open`, `unshare`, `setns`, `kexec_*`, `keyctl`).
